verdicts.opus: B and C both used the measured title-match series (474→821, flat 2020-23, sharp 2024-25 rise) and the scenario range (central 864/908/951, bounds 304–1,598 by 2028). B recomputed every ratio, delta and fold error correctly and read the marginal backtest advantage, though its untagged verdict range zeroes its verdict score. C misreported the 2024→2025 jump as 73% instead of 39%. A offered labelled guesses on a different scale, and D declined to answer, so neither gives a decision-maker a usable range.
verdicts.gpt: A is the strongest decision aid: it gives a reproducible historical series and a clearly bounded three-year scenario, while acknowledging the forecast’s weak validation. D offers deeper follow-up work, but its untagged verdict figures and unsupported full-coverage label weaken trust; B is careful but cannot quantify the answer, and C relies on estimates.
